items are used just once and then discarded. <break time="0.8s" /> Do you ever stop to think about where these plastic items go after you throw them away. <break time="0.8s" /> Recycling can help reduce the amount of plastic in our landfills. <break time="0.8s" /> However, less than ten percent of the worlds plastic waste has been recycled so far. <break time="0.8s" /> Often, plastic waste is moved to places where it is just dumped or burned. <break time="0.8s" /> Furthermore, between 8 and 14 million metric tons of plastic end up in the ocean every year. <break time="0.8s" /> This puts many marine species in danger. <break time="0.8s" /> With this in mind, scientists are turning to mealworms. <break time="0.8s" /> Mealworms are the larvae of a certain species of beetle. <break time="0.8s" /> Special bacteria live inside them. <break time="0.8s" /> These bacteria can break down plastic. <break time="0.8s" /> This means that mealworms can actually feed on plastic. <break time="0.8s" /> Scientists are now looking for ways to cultivate the bacteria outside of mealworms. <break time="0.8s" /> They also want to speed up the process by which the bacteria break down plastic. <break time="0.8s" /> This may help us keep our landfills plastic free. <break time="0.8s" /> Mining and other industries are causing soil pollution across the globe. <break time="0.8s" /> Although polluted soil can be dug up and transported to a landfill, this process is expensive. <break time="0.8s" /> Moreover, it only moves the problem to another area and does not really solve it. <break time="0.8s" /> Fortunately, there is an eco friendly and cost effective way to restore polluted soil, planting willow trees. <break time="0.8s" /> These amazing trees have extensive and well developed root systems. <break time="0.8s" /> As a result, they naturally extract a wide range of harmful materials from the soil. <break time="0.8s" /> They can also grow quickly, even in soil with a high acidity level or a lot of heavy metals in it. <break time="0.8s" /> Research on the effectiveness of using willow trees for this purpose is in development. <break time="0.8s" /> Scientists have found that some species of willow trees are able to absorb harmful materials better than others. <break time="0.8s" /> Therefore, this promising area should be further explored to find out which trees are the most effective. <break time="0.8s" /> In time, we may be able to clean up our land with willow trees. <break time="0.8s" /> Statistics show that about thirty to forty percent of people in the world drink coffee each day. <break time="0.8s" /> The coffee making process, however, generates used coffee grounds, which are normally sent to landfills. <break time="0.8s" /> There, they can create a harmful greenhouse gas. <break time="0.8s" /> Unfortunately, there is no way to stop everyone in the world from drinking coffee. <break time="0.8s" /> However, we can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by turning used coffee grounds into biofuel. <break time="0.8s" /> Biofuel is a natural fuel that is made from plant or animal sources. <break time="0.8s" /> Researchers have found that they can grow algae on old coffee grounds without adding any other nutrients. <break time="0.8s" /> If these algae are exposed to twenty hours of light and four hours of darkness each day, they eventually produce high quality biofuel. <break time="0.8s" /> The biofuel is renewable and sustainable, and it creates only a small amount of emissions. <break time="0.8s" /> These are just a few solutions we can find in nature. <break time="0.8s" /> There could be many more possible solutions to the problems we currently face. <break time="0.8s" /> It seems that Mother Nature has given us one more chance. <break time="0.8s" /> In return, we need to look for more ways to keep the environment healthy and clean. <break time="0.8s" /> If we do, the future of our planet may be bright after all.
